subject: Pricing proposal: redundant GPU pools vs active routing — multi-region asks
messages:
From: Katherine Marsh <km@nimbusretail.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity: multi-region redundancy options & DR credit ask

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the numbers on our side and are evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a 12-month reserved commit that must span US and EU regions.

Two quick asks to help our procurement and SRE teams evaluate:

- Can you outline the cost and SLA differences between (A) deploying separate, regional GPU pools with passive replication (active-passive failover) versus (B) an active-active setup with cross-region routing?
- Do you offer DR/failover credits or a Disaster Recovery Allowance (DRA) for cross-region failover events? Our procurement wants a credit policy for the first 72 hours of a failover event.
- What's the replication surcharge (if any) and are there discounts for committing capacity across regions (blended pricing)?
- We need throughput guarantees: P99 latency target ~50ms for our 2k TPS peak in-region. How do you map that to GPU pool sizing?

I've attached a small workload sample (inventory_workload_v2.csv) to show seq lengths and QPS distribution.

Goal: procurement needs an internal comparison of pricing and credits by EOD next Tuesday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,

Katherine Marsh
Director, Cloud Infrastructure
Nimbus Retail

Lauren — quick pricing and architectural options below. I attached a worked model (pricing_model_v1.xlsx) for the numbers. High-level options:

Option A — Regional pools (active-passive failover)- Setup: Separate committed GPU pools in US and EU. Cross-region replication is optional (snapshot/KV-sync).
- Cost: Base committed GPU-month price = $8,200 / GPU-month (single-region list).
- Replication surcharge (optional incremental state mirroring): +12% of committed price (covers KV sync + storage + replication bandwidth).
- Failover handling: Active-passive failover uses standby capacity in target region; during failover we provide a Disaster Recovery Allowance (DRA) credit policy: first 24 hours free, additional hours billed at 50% rate of committed price.
- Pros: lower steady-state cost; 
- Cons: failover can incure cold-start impacts and cross-region egress (customer pays egress).

Option B — Active-active with cross-region routing- Setup: Mirror traffic across two active pools with regional routing and automatic cross-region routing on degradation.
- Cost: Base committed GPU-month price (blended) = $8,200 / GPU-month + active-active uplift of 20% = $9,840 / GPU-month.
- Replication surcharge: included in uplift (no separate +12%).
- Failover handling: near-zero failover impact; we offer a 99.9% availability SLA and an SLO mapping to P99 latency in-region.
- Pros: better availability and smoother failover;
- Cons: higher committed cost (full uplift).

Discount tiers (applies to committed GPUs, blended across regions):
- 10–29 GPUs: 5% off list
- 30–74 GPUs: 12% off list
- 75+ GPUs: 20% off list

Examples (blended, 12-month):
- 30 GPUs US + 20 GPUs EU (50 GPU blended): list base = $8,200 => blended list ~ $8,200. After 12% discount = $7,216 GPU-month. Active-active uplift +20% => $8,659 GPU-month. Replication surcharge for Option A = +12% on list before discount.

Throughput/latency mapping (ballpark) for their 2k TPS peak, P99 ~50ms target (depends on model, seq length):
- Conservative sizing: 1 GPU for ~40–60 concurrent RPS for medium-sized LLMs at 2k seq tokens average => 40 GPUs (in-region) to keep P99 <= 50ms with continuous batching disabled.
- Aggressive batching + KV caching: 1 GPU for ~80–120 RPS => 20–25 GPUs (but more variability at tail).

Operational notes:
- Burst capacity: we can enable burst pools (pay-as-you-go) for short spikes; burst is billed at on-demand rate (no discount).
- Cross-region egress is billed to customer; recommend include estimated egress allowance in commercial.

Failover credits: we can be flexible. For a sales-approved term, we can propose "first 72 hours per year covered as DRA" for committed deals >= 50 GPUs with a 12-month commit — but that will reduce discount by ~2–4 points in the blended price. The attached spreadsheet models both scenarios.

Next steps: Marcus, can you run two blended scenarios (A and B) for 30US+20EU with and without the 72-hour DRA and show net MSP price and annualized savings? Dev — can you sanity-check the conservative GPU sizing above against inventory_workload_v2.csv?

-Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Katherine Marsh <km@nimbusretail.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-23T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity: multi-region redundancy options & DR credit ask

Karthik / Lauren — thanks for the detailed breakdown. A few follow-ups and pushbacks from procurement/SRE after reviewing the numbers: 

- The active-active uplift looks expensive for our forecasted traffic. Nimbus is prepared to commit to 12 months and a blended 50 GPU baseline, but we need a better blended discount than 12% if we are asked to pay replication/active-active uplift. We're asking for a 20% total discount on blended spend if we commit 50 GPUs across regions.
- The DRA ask: procurement insists on 72 hours per year as unpaid/funded by vendor for a multi-region outage (not just 24 hours). If you offer 72 hours, we'll accept active-passive.
- Cold-start impact: SRE wants details on how much extra latency we should expect during cross-region failover and whether you can offer a short warmup window (pre-warming) during failover without billing at full rate.
- Request: can you include a clause that caps cross-region egress at a negotiated monthly allowance? They'd like egress to be predictable.

If you can present a clean term sheet that includes: (a) a blended 50 GPU price with a 20% discount, (b) 72-hour DRA per year for free, (c) egress cap X TB/month, and (d) an option to pilot active-active for 30 days at the active-active uplift rate pro-rated, procurement will move quickly.

Katherine

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: Katherine Marsh <km@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-24T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Revised commercial proposal and next steps (Nimbus Retail)

Katherine — thanks for the clarity. We've modeled your asks and produced a short term sheet. Attached: proposed_term_sheet_20270824.pdf and SLA_99th_traffic.pdf. Key points (summary):

- Commit: 12 months, blended 50 GPUs (30 US / 20 EU).
- Base list price (pre-discount): $8,200 / GPU-month.
- Discount: 15% standard (we can flex to 18% for an approved commercial sign-off by our revenue ops team). We cannot go to 20% without exec approval; I'll escalate if required.
- Failover/DRA: We will include 72 hours of DRA per calendar year for the contracted term for this deal (first 72 hours of failover covered at no additional charge). Additional failover hours billed at 50% of blended GPU-month pro-rata.
- Replication / Active-active: Active-active option available at +20% uplift over the post-discount blended price (replication included).
- Egress: We will include a negotiated egress allowance of 10 TB / month across regions for the first year. Overages billed at our standard egress rate; we will include a monthly cap trigger to notify both teams.
- Pilot: 30-day active-active pilot available at pro-rated active-active uplift. The pilot will have a reduced commit requirement (15 GPUs) as a canary.
- Throughput sizing: Dev validated conservative sizing of 40 GPUs for your 2k TPS P99 ~50ms target; aggressive path at 25 GPUs with KV caching and batched inference. See SLA_99th_traffic.pdf for baseline tests and assumptions.

Impact to price (summary example):
- Blended 50 GPUs, post-discount at 18% => $6,724 GPU-month. Active-active uplift (+20%) => $8,069 GPU-month.
- With 72-hour DRA included, our commercial team accounts for an incremental margin reduction; the 18% discount is our concession to balance the DRA and the egress allowance.

Next steps:
1) I will escalate to finance/ops for an exec exception to push discount to 20% if you confirm NDA/PO terms.
2) Marcus will publish the final term sheet and an invoice schedule if you confirm the blended 50 GPU commitment.
3) If accepted, we will provision a 30-day pilot (pro-rated active-active) and schedule a technical runbook review with your SREs on pre-warm and failover behaviors.

Attachments: proposed_term_sheet_20270824.pdf; SLA_99th_traffic.pdf

Please let me know if the 18% (with a fast exec path to 20%) is acceptable — happy to jump on a 30-min call to close.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
